run.question: 配置的业务数据库里有哪些表？orders 表里每种 status 的订单各有多少条、failed 占比多少？请用数据库只读查询工具核实后回答。

report.summary: The configured business database (dialect mysql, target m0-otel-20260909, source otel-demo) exposes exactly one read-visible table, testdb.orders, with columns id (int, PK), customer (varchar(40)), status (varchar(16)) and amount (decimal(10,2)). Grouping the table by status returned three distinct values: paid 144, failed 72, refunded 24, for a total of 240 rows with no NULL status. A second aggregate query confirmed total 240, failed 72 and a failed share of 30.00%. All values are the database as read at 2026-11-20T21:24:00–21:24:02Z, i.e. after the authorized incident window, not a historical snapshot.

claims.text: Listing the tables of the configured MySQL database with schema omitted (configured database) returned one table only: schema testdb, name orders, type table. No other table or view was returned.

The table testdb.orders has 4 columns: id (int, NOT NULL, primary key PRIMARY unique), customer (varchar(40), nullable), status (varchar(16), nullable), amount (decimal(10,2), nullable); it has no foreign keys.
GROUP BY status on orders returned exactly three status groups: status=paid with 144 rows, status=failed with 72 rows, status=refunded with 24 rows (3 rows returned, none omitted, not truncated).
A single aggregate over orders returned total=240 rows, failed_cnt=72, failed_pct=30.00, and null_status=0, confirming failed orders are 72 of 240 = exactly 30.00% of the table.

status is defined nullable in the table schema, but the aggregate query counted null_status=0, so all 240 rows carry one of the three observed status values and the percentage denominator is complete for those values.

gaps: The table list is scoped to the configured database only; with schema omitted, MySQL listing covers just that database, so tables in other schemas on the same server were not enumerated and remain unknown.

All query results are the database's state at query time (2026-11-20T21:24:00Z–21:24:02Z, per the tool notes 'the database as it is now, not as it was in the authorized window ending 2026-11-20T21:23:57Z'); historical order-status distribution inside the authorized window 2026-11-19T21:23:57Z–2026-11-20T21:23:57Z was not reconstructed, and the schema has no timestamp column to do so.
Whether any table or row is invisible to the read-only account (privilege or row-filtering) cannot be verified from these results.
The business meaning of status='failed' (payment failure vs. fulfillment failure) is not recorded in the table or in the returned evidence.
next_steps: If the failed-order share matters for an incident assessment, confirm with the application owner which system writes orders.status and whether 30.00% failed is the normal steady state or a deviation, since no historical baseline for this table was available.
If other schemas may hold business tables, list them explicitly by schema name with database_sql_list_tables(schema=...) to complete the inventory.

query.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY cnt DESC

SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, SUM(CASE WHEN status='failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_cnt, ROUND(100*SUM(CASE WHEN status='failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS failed_pct, SUM(CASE WHEN status IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_status FROM orders
